A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same SVL study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H support a reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original SVL experiments in Section 5 and Appendix A, including zero-shot classification, captioning, downstream tasks, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains these original empirical results, including classification and captioning results in Tables 1–4 and supplementary experiments in Tables 8–11.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains identical MTA losses, Rep-VLI inference, I-LIF processing, and Spike-driven PointFormer architecture. The multimodal training procedure in Appendix B is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is identical, including ModelNet40, ScanObjectNN, Objaverse/Objaverse-LVIS, KITTI, SemanticKITTI, DVS datasets, Synthia 4D, and the ScanNet qualitative example.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding comparison, including OpenShape, ULIP, ULIP-2 and SpikeCLIP in Table 1, captioning baselines in Table 2, and supplementary comparisons in Tables 8–9 and 13.

E3.justification: The versions specify identical data splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, timestep settings, training budgets, and testing procedures in Section 5 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The loss and timestep ablations in Section 5.3, efficiency and temporal analyses in Appendix A, voxel-size and point-density studies, CLIP-size analysis, and qualitative cases are all unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Their statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative outputs match, including 85.4% ModelNet40 zero-shot accuracy in Table 1, 80.05% Synthia 4D mIoU in Table 9, and the responses in Figure 2 and Tables 12–13.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is identical, including neuron and alignment equations, Rep-VLI formulations, the energy model in Appendix C, and the gradient derivation in Appendix G.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient open-world 3D understanding, MTA, Rep-VLI, downstream performance, and the first fully spike-driven point Transformer.

C2.justification: Interpretations of alignment, efficiency, temporal processing, and encoder scaling are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitation concerning validation at restricted model scales.

D1.justification: Implementation and preprocessing descriptions, multimodal training details, hyperparameters, architecture configurations, and the code-access link are identical, including Tables 14–18.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and positioning relative to prior SNNs and vision-language methods are unchanged. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 17 May 2026 to v3 dated 4 August 2026, and the PDF title metadata is updated to match the displayed title. The displayed title, authors, manuscript prose, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp moves slightly right and downward. All figures, tables, and body layouts remain unchanged; rendered pages 2–20 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, results, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical throughout the main text and Appendices A–H. Updating document metadata and repositioning the arXiv stamp produces no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
